personal_account.lender_description: The author thinks the lender was a micro-lender; identity unconfirmed
reported_sequence: Sued over a debt in what he describes as the lowest court
Served a summons with a small canary-yellow note stapled to it, offering resolution outside court by calling the lawyers' collection phone number
Mediation was scheduled that day in the courtroom, with the judge and mediators present
The judge said those attending could trust the mediators
Repeatedly said he did not want mediation
Understood nonappearance could lead to default and could not obtain an opt-out while unrepresented
Appeared in person to decline and told the judge he was there under duress
Recalls that the case then went away
reported_concerns: Experienced the proposed discussion as assuming the claimant's records were correct and directing him toward payment arrangements
Saw no meaningful opportunity in that setting to challenge the records or the fundamentals of the claimant's case
Believed the mediator would lead him into acting as a witness against his own interests about documents prepared by someone absent from court
Interpreted this as giving the claimant's lawyers an extraordinary advantage
Understood the phone number on the canary-yellow note to be for debt collection
Believed counsel could avoid his personal appearance
Interpreted the added appearance as an opportunity to obtain default before trial
unknowns: Case date, court, precinct, and docket

research_limitations: JP1 is a published comparison, not an identified court in the recollection
Current rules do not establish historical governing rules without a case date
No general exemption from personal attendance based solely on having counsel is established
No finding of manufactured defaults, debt validity, sanction legality, or judicial misconduct
